In color theory, it combines all colors in the visible spectrum. While white isn’t included on the color wheel, it plays an important role in color mixing, creating lighter, softer shades of colors. White creates contrast and balance in UI designs while promoting a clean, minimalistic aesthetic.What does white look like on digital screens?White is defined by the following color codes and values to ensure consistency across various digital platforms and devices.HEX code: #FFFFFFRGB value: 100% red, 100% green, and 100% blueAccessibility considerations play a crucial role in UX and UI design color choices. Figma offers plugins in the Community to make sure your designs meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines.How should I effectively use white in UI design?Here are some ways to incorporate white into your UI designs:Enhance readability. Using white as a background color can help make text and buttons pop, improving readability and ensuring users can easily digest information on a page.Create harmony. White space can help create balance on a page and properly direct a user’s focus from one element to another. It also creates a clean and harmonious interface, reducing user fatigue and delivering an enjoyable experience.Inspire cleanliness. White is often associated with cleanliness and freshness, creating a simple and minimalistic aesthetic. It conveys feelings of safety, making it great for designs in the medical and health space.Keep in mind that color and its meaning can change from culture to culture—and at any given time. If you are designing for a global audience, research color considerations for your specific regions.What are similar colors to white?For variations within the same bright spectrum as white, consider:Off-white (#F2F0EF) has a slight gray undertone, giving it a soft and cool appearance.Ivory (#FFFFE3) brings a warmer touch with a hint of yellow undertones.Seashell (#FFF1E7) has a slightly pink undertone, radiating the delicacy of seashells.Cream (#FDFBD4) adds a touch of warmth with a pale yellow hue.What colors go with white?To complement white, consider pairing it with:Black (#000000) offers a classic and timeless look when paired with white.Mint green (#ADEBB3) provides a touch of softness to create an airy and tender feel.Misty blue (#B5C7EB) embodies tranquility, creating a calm and serene atmosphere.Brown (#895129) has rich hues that elicit a warm, natural color palette.Other colors worth considering include sage green for an earthy color combination, periwinkle for a whimsical feel, and baby blue to ground white’s freshness.What colors conflict with white?While white is clean, it may clash with:Cool gray (#CBCBCB) has a light gray hue, which can look dull when paired with white.Neon green (#2CFF05) creates a harsh contrast next to white, which can be visually straining.Yellow (#FFFF00) may appear too bright next to stark white, creating a jarring effect.Cyan (#00FFFF) can feel overwhelming next to white due to its striking contrast.What does white symbolize? While white commonly represents purity and innocence in Western ceremonies like weddings and baptisms, it carries meanings of death and renewal in Eastern traditions.In color psychology, white can evoke feelings of peace and tranquility, creating a calming atmosphere. In some contexts, white can also trigger feelings of emptiness and isolation, particularly in stark, all-white environments such as empty hospital rooms.In UI design, white is highly versatile and effective for making information stand out. It brings harmony to design interfaces, guiding users through visual content and creating a visually pleasing user experience.What’s the history of white? White was one of the first colors used in prehistoric cave paintings, where the pigments were made from minerals like chalk, limestone, calcite, and gypsum. For example, the famous Lascaux cave in France revealed drawings of bulls and other animals using these white materials.Ancient Greeks, Romans, and Egyptians also used white pigments in art, sculpture, pottery, and architecture. Many of these ancient civilizations associated white with purity, sacrifice, and godliness, making it a prominent color for priests’ gowns and togas. Today, white continues to hold the same significance in many religions and cultures around the world.The 20th century brought more advancements in white pigments as more substances became accessible. Titanium dioxide, for example, revolutionized the production of white paint and became the primary pigment used. White also plays a crucial role in color mixing today. It can add a touch of brightness to any color, combine with black to make various shades of gray, and add softness to colors to produce pastel hues.Color variationsShadesCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#E3E3E3Copy Hex:#C6C6C6Copy Hex:#AAAAAACopy Hex:#8E8E8ECopy Hex:#717171Copy Hex:#555555Copy Hex:#393939TintsCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#F2F2F2Copy Hex:#F2F2F2Copy Hex:#F2F2F2Copy Hex:#F2F2F2Copy Hex:#F2F2F2Copy Hex:#F2F2F2Copy Hex:#F2F2F2TonesCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#808080Copy Hex:#808080Copy Hex:#808080Copy Hex:#808080Copy Hex:#808080Copy Hex:#808080Copy Hex:#808080HuesCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFColor harmoniesComplementaryCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFSplitCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFMonochromaticCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#CCCCCCCopy Hex:#FFFFFFAnalogousCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFTriadicCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFSquareCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCustom palettesSalt And PepperCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#D4D4D4Copy Hex:#B3B3B3Copy Hex:#2B2B2BUrban VogueCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#D1D1D1Copy Hex:#C25F5FCopy Hex:#703030Pastel SoftnessCopy Hex:#FFFFFFCopy Hex:#FAF6CFCopy Hex:#C9F1E2Copy Hex:#DACFFAAccessibilityContrast checkerContrast 1Large Text#FFFFFFNormal TextHow you design, align, and build matters.
